title: Momentum and Collisions
subtitle: Give carts momentum, make them collide, and discover what stays the same.
objectives: Calculate momentum as p = m × v, including its direction.
Use conservation of total momentum to predict the outcome of a collision.
Distinguish perfectly inelastic collisions (carts stick) from elastic ones (carts bounce).

derived.expr: d.collides ? simkit.physics.collide1D(s.mA, s.vA, s.mB, s.vB, s.type === 'sticky' ? 0 : 1).v1 : s.vA
d.collides ? simkit.physics.collide1D(s.mA, s.vA, s.mB, s.vB, s.type === 'sticky' ? 0 : 1).v2 : s.vB

formulas.meaning: Momentum; the sign gives the direction (right is +).
Total momentum of the two-cart system.
Perfectly inelastic: the carts move together.

debrief: In every collision the total momentum stayed the same. Sticky collisions lose kinetic energy; elastic ones keep it.

levels.title: Momentum of one cart
levels.goal: Give the red cart a momentum of +12 kg·m/s (to the right).
hints: Find a mass and a velocity whose product is 12, for example $3\,\text{kg} \times 4\,\text{m/s}$.

feedback.say: Right size, wrong direction: positive momentum points to the right.

levels.solutionText: Any pair with $m \times v = 12$ works: $2 \times 6$, $3 \times 4$, $4 \times 3$ or $6 \times 2$.
levels.explain: Momentum is the product of mass and velocity, so many combinations give the same momentum.

levels.title: Relative momentum
levels.goal: The blue cart has 4 kg·m/s to the right. Give the red cart three times that momentum, pointing the opposite way.
hints: Opposite direction means negative: you need $p = -12\,\text{kg·m/s}$.

feedback.say: The size is right, but it must point left (negative velocity).

levels.explain: Direction is part of momentum: −12 kg·m/s is just as large as +12 but points left.

levels.title: Perfectly inelastic stop
levels.goal: The carts stick together on impact. Set them up so they collide and come to a complete stop.
hints: After a sticky collision the carts share one velocity: $v = \dfrac{p_\text{total}}{m_\text{red} + m_\text{blue}}$.
To end at rest the total momentum must be zero, and the carts must move towards each other.

feedback.say: These carts never meet: the red cart must move right faster than the blue cart.
Total momentum is {pTotal} kg·m/s, so the joined carts keep moving.

levels.solutionText: Make the momenta equal and opposite: $3 \times 2 = +6$ and $2 \times (-3) = -6$. The total is 0, so the stuck carts stop.
levels.explain: Zero total momentum before the collision means zero after it, so the joined carts stop. Press Run collision to watch.

levels.title: Predict the final velocity
levels.goal: A 3 kg red cart moving at 4 m/s hits a 1 kg blue cart at rest. They stick together. What is their velocity afterwards?
hints: The same momentum is shared by the combined $4\,\text{kg}$.

feedback.say: 12 is the total momentum in kg·m/s. Divide by the total mass.
That is the red cart's speed before the collision.

levels.explain: Momentum is conserved: $12\,\text{kg·m/s}$ shared by $4\,\text{kg}$ gives $3\,\text{m/s}$. Run the collision to see it.

levels.title: Elastic transfer
levels.goal: In a bouncing (elastic) collision, make the red cart stop dead while the blue cart leaves at exactly 4 m/s.
hints: If the red cart stops, all of its momentum is handed to the blue cart.
Kinetic energy is also conserved, which only works out when the two masses are equal.
With equal masses the blue cart leaves with the red cart's original velocity.

feedback.say: The carts do not collide yet.
The red cart stops, but blue leaves at {vB2} m/s.
After the collision the red cart moves at {vA2} m/s.

levels.solutionText: Equal masses swap velocities in an elastic collision. Set the red cart to 2 kg (same as blue) moving at 4 m/s.
levels.explain: Momentum and kinetic energy are both conserved; with equal masses the moving cart hands over all its motion.
